requirement:
The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
in `used`, as described in {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.mcp.description`.
rationale:
The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]` covers each obligation of `requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions`:

- **First result carries `instructions`, even when empty.** In the `session` conversation, a `search_text` for "absent" returns no matches. The test reads `empty["instructions"]` as a string. In the `peer` conversation, an empty `search_structure` result asserts `matches == []` and `instructions` equal to the earlier string. A non-empty first result in the `fresh` conversation also asserts `hits["instructions"] == instructions`.
- **Text and structural searches share the rule.** The `session` and `fresh` conversations cover `search_text`. The `peer` conversation covers `search_structure`.
- **Each conversation gets its own first delivery.** The `session`, `fresh` and `peer` conversations each receive instructions on their own first successful search.
- **Failed searches leave instructions for the first successful delivery.** The very first dispatch in `session` is an invalid regex, `"("`, which is asserted to be an error. The next successful search, "absent", still carries `instructions`. A structural-search failure is not tested separately. The implementation (`Pages::search` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/pages.rs`) uses one shared `first_search && index == 0` path for both tools, so this is not a separate behavior.
- **Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.** Four asserted cases:
  - A later `peer` text search has no `instructions`.
  - The `fresh` conversation's `get_next_page` result has none.
  - A second `session` search for "hit" has none.
  - The `session` continuation page, `second`, has none.
- **Instructions explain `finish_search` and the `used` tags**, as described in the cited `finish_search.mcp.description`. The test asserts that the instructions contain the phrases "Before submitting, close every delivered search page", `finish_search`, "tags for excerpts you relied on without a separate source read", "used:[] if none qualify, including an empty result" and "without reading more source". These cover when to call `finish_search` and which tags go in `used`. The exact wording is the subject of `first_search.instructions.content`, which the same test also marks, so it is not reassessed here.

Other tests, such as the pages test and the redaction test, add further assertions that only the first page carries instructions. I found no unacknowledged gap.

text: The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
> `Close a delivered search and record dependencies for snippets you used to
> justify your conclusion without an additional source read. search_id is the
> result's UUID and used is an array of its short entry tags, e.g.
> whose source you also read may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use
> used:[] when no entries qualify, including an empty search. Every delivered
> search must be finished before submission. The result is {search_id,
> finished:true}; no additional source is delivered.`
